questions.q: Which region, a semi-desert stretch beyond the Cape's mountain passes, does the Court tie to sweet fortified wines and brandy?
questions.exp: The Klein Karoo, the Little Karoo, is the semi-desert region the Court files for sweet fortified wines and brandy: Calitzdorp makes the country's finest Port-style wines from Touriga Nacional and Tinta Barocca, and Muscadel and the brandy still are long traditions there. The Coastal Region and the Cape South Coast are cooled by the sea and grow table wine.

questions.q: Elim, the windswept ward near the continent's southernmost point, lies inside which district from the Court's Certified list?
questions.exp: Elim is a ward of the Cape Agulhas district, on a windswept plain near Africa's southernmost point, and its Sauvignon Blanc is severe and saline. The Court adds Cape Agulhas and Overberg at the Certified level to the Introductory Elgin and Walker Bay, all of them districts of the Cape South Coast region.

questions.q: From which compass direction does the Cape Doctor blow onto the shore and the vineyards through spring and summer?
questions.exp: The Cape Doctor is the Court's strong, dry south-easterly, blowing in across False Bay from spring into summer; it dries the canopy, keeps rot and other pests in check and cools the vineyards near the coast. Its cooling partner is the Benguela Current, the frigid Atlantic water that runs up the west coast from Antarctica.

questions.q: What does the Court give as the objective of South Africa's Old Vine Project?
opts: To preserve old vines and grow more of them sustainably
To replace old vines with virus-free modern clones
To classify the Cape's estates by the age of their cellars
To set minimum prices for old-vine bulk wine
questions.exp: The Old Vine Project sets out to preserve old vineyards and to promote sustainable viticulture that will create more old vines; since 2018 its Certified Heritage Vineyards seal carries the planting date of a vineyard of 35 years or more on the bottle. Old Chenin Blanc bush vines in the Swartland and beyond are its best-known cause.

questions.q: A guest wants a Pinot Noir from the Hemel-en-Aarde made by one of the producers the Court lists. Which name do you offer?
questions.exp: Hamilton Russell Vineyards, founded in 1975 in the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley of Walker Bay, proved the Cape could make serious Pinot Noir and Chardonnay and bottles only those two under its own name. Graham Beck is Robertson's Cap Classique house, Klein Constantia revived Vin de Constance, and Mulderbosch is a Stellenbosch name.

questions.q: Which Robertson house on the Court's producer list is the Cape's best-known specialist in Cap Classique?
questions.exp: Graham Beck, on the lime-rich soils of Robertson, is the Cap Classique specialist whose non-vintage Brut was poured at Nelson Mandela's inauguration in 1994. Cap Classique, the Court's Certified term, is South African sparkling wine made by the traditional method, with at least twelve months on the lees.

questions.q: Which political system, and the sanctions it drew, shut South African wine out of most export markets until the early 1990s?
questions.exp: Apartheid and the trade sanctions against it kept Cape wine off most foreign shelves until the system was dismantled; the 1994 election reopened the markets and exports grew many times over. The Court's History row sets this beside van der Stel's Dutch settlement, phylloxera in 1886, the Anglo-Boer War and the KWV.

questions.q: A guest wants a world class Chenin Blanc of honeyed depth from old dry-farmed bush vines, at a fraction of a top Vouvray's price. Which Cape district do you steer them to?
questions.exp: The Court frames Cape wines, from sparkling to light and crisp to rich and intense, as world class recommendations from an undervalued area, and Swartland Chenin Blanc from old dry-farmed bush vines is the clearest case of that value. Elgin is cool apple country for Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay, Robertson's lime soils are known for Chardonnay and Cap Classique, and Cape Agulhas for saline Sauvignon Blanc.
